flags.quote: Taking the pawn on h6 with your bishop is a blunder because the pawn was undefended.
flags.critique: You just told me taking a free pawn is a blunder *because it was undefended*. That's backwards — undefended is why I'd take it, not why it's bad. The real story is the bishop gets chased: Rh7, then I lose h3 and Black's rook wakes up on the h-file, and +2.8 becomes equal. Don't praise the capture in the same breath you call it a blunder.

flags.quote: Moving your bishop to b8 leaves your pawn hanging to the white bishop.
flags.critique: h6 was already hanging to Bf4 before Bb8 — Ba7 never defended it. Then White takes that 'hanging' pawn and you call *that* a 277cp blunder. So which is it? The lesson I needed was that Bb8 is a passive wait while Rd4 hits the bishop on f4, not a fake 'you hung a pawn' story that the next move contradicts.

flags.quote: Moving your rook to h7 is the strongest move because your rook gets a semi-open file.
flags.critique: The rook went to h7 to *attack the bishop that just stole h6*. That's the trap. 'Semi-open file' is a file-label slapped on a tactic. If I'm the one who blundered Bxh6, this is the sentence that should make me wince — instead I learn nothing about why taking h6 failed.

flags.quote: You are still winning, but moving your bishop to e3 leaves your king trapped on the back rank. A better move would have been moving your queen to c2 because you can likely skewer the black queen and the black pawn.
flags.critique: Be3 *attacks the queen on d4*. That's the move. My king is not newly trapped on the back rank — f2/g2/h3 are still there — and king_safer in the reasons contradicts back_rank anyway. Qc2 'likely skewering the queen and a pawn' is invented: from c2 you don't skewer Qd4. Stop hallucinating tactics and tell me I kicked the queen.

flags.quote: Taking the pawn on d5 with your e-pawn is the strongest move because you take the defender of the black c6-knight.
flags.critique: A black pawn on d5 captures toward c4 and e4. It does not defend the knight on c6. You just taught me a geometry that isn't chess. This is a central exchange — say that, don't invent a removed-defender tactic on a piece the pawn never protected.

flags.quote: Taking the pawn on d5 with your f6-knight is the strongest move because the pawn was undefended.
flags.critique: Nc3 defends d5. This is a recapture, not a free pawn, and wins_material is a lie. If every even trade is 'the piece was undefended,' I will start hanging pieces on purpose thinking I'm winning them.

flags.quote: Taking the pawn on d3 with your queen is an inaccuracy because you pin the bishop to the queen and the pawn was undefended.
flags.critique: Those are the *features of my capture*, used as the reason it's bad. Taking a hanging pawn is not an inaccuracy *because* the pawn was hanging. If Bd4 was better, tell me the idea — pin on the a7–g1 diagonal, pressure on f2/c5 — not a word salad that makes the good part of Qxd3 sound like the crime.

flags.quote: Taking the pawn on f4 with your g-pawn is the strongest move because you take the defender of the white bishop.
flags.critique: White's f4 pawn captures on e5 and g5. It does not defend the bishop on e3 (pawns don't protect backwards). Same removed-defender bug as exd5. This is a pawn-break recapture that opens the f-file — teach the structure, not a defender that isn't there.

flags.quote: Moving your c5-bishop to a7 is the strongest move because it saves your a7-bishop from capture.
flags.critique: The bishop is on c5 until it lands on a7. You named it by the destination, then said it saved itself. b4 kicked the Italian bishop; Ba7 is the retreat. 'Saves your a7-bishop' is a copy bug that sounds like a joke.

flags.quote: Moving your rook to d7 is a mistake, but moving your rook to b3 would be better because it gives your rook a semi-open file.
flags.critique: 162 centipawns for a file label? The rook on d3 was chewing the third rank (a3, Be3, g3, h3). Rd7 just walks off that job; Rb3 keeps the rook active against b4. 'Semi-open file' is what you say when you don't know why the engine screamed. Also 'is a mistake, but' is clumsy, and saves_piece in the reasons is false — nothing was taking that rook.

flags.quote: Moving your g1-knight to f3 is playable, but moving your pawn to d4 would be better because you can likely take a pawn.
flags.critique: After 1.e3 e5, d4 challenges e5. I cannot 'likely take a pawn' — Black recaptures or plays Nc6. That weasel 'likely' is how you invent a capture that isn't there. Teach the reversed-French idea: hit the center immediately, not a phantom snack.

flags.quote: Taking the knight on d5 with your e6-bishop is the strongest move because the knight was undefended.
flags.critique: Qd1 defends d5. Third recapture in a row sold as winning a hanging piece. I already know to take back — I need 'this is an even exchange on d5,' not another undefended lie.

flags.quote: Taking the queen on d1 with your a1-rook is the strongest move because the queen was undefended.
flags.critique: Re1 defends d1. This is a queen trade recapture after Be3 kicked Qd4, not winning a loose queen. wins_material on Qxd1/Raxd1 is the same recapture bug with a bigger piece name so it sounds more impressive and more wrong.

flags.quote: Moving your pawn to b4 is the strongest move.
flags.critique: This is the point of a3: kick the c5-bishop, grab space, maybe trap it off a7. You gave me a period. If you only speak when there's a tactic, I'm going to think pawn storms don't count as ideas.

flags.quote: Moving your rook to d3 is the strongest move.
flags.critique: The rook attacks Be3 and the whole third rank. That's a 1200 lesson (put the rook on a rank with targets). Empty 'strongest move' after you just spent the middlegame drowning me in fake pins is insulting.

flags.quote: Moving your king to f7 is the strongest move.
flags.critique: Queens are off. The king walks toward the center. That's *the* endgame rule you should be drilling, and the hidden reason is pawn_shield — jargon for the opposite idea. Don't call king centralization 'shielding' or say nothing.

flags.quote: Taking the bishop on c6 with your b-pawn is the strongest move because the bishop was undefended.
flags.critique: Recapture, not a free bishop — you just lost the knight on c6. The reasons pile doubled, isolated, *and* backward pawns onto a must-take, then the sentence ignores all of them. Either teach 'you recapture and accept doubled c-pawns' or shut up about the structure. This does both and neither.

flags.quote: Moving your f8-rook to e8 is the strongest move because it overloads the white queen.
flags.critique: Overloads *what*? The queen isn't named as defending two things I can actually take. If you can't say 'the queen has to watch d4 and the back rank,' don't drop a tactic word and smirk. 58cp swing marked best with a vocabulary flex.

flags.quote: Moving your pawn to g5 is playable, but moving your pawn to f5 would be better.
flags.critique: Better *why*? Empty reasons, no because. f5 vs g5 is a pawn-break choice next to the kings — space, fixing White's bishop, king restriction. 'Would be better.' is a shrug, not coaching.

flags.quote: Moving your king to e6 is the strongest move.
flags.critique: Same empty verdict, and the reasons are king_more_exposed *and* pawn_shield on a best king march. In this endgame the king *should* be 'exposed' in the center. You're tagging the right move with the scare-reason you'd use for walking into a mate net.

flags.quote: Moving your pawn to e3 is the strongest move because you claim more of the center.
flags.critique: e3 is Van't Kruijs, a modest pawn that gives up the usual +0.25 first-move edge. Calling it the strongest center-claim is the same sentence you'll use for e4, d4, and d3. I know e3 doesn't 'claim the center' the way e4 does — don't template-farm the opening.

flags.quote: Moving your queen to d4 is playable, but moving your a8-rook to d8 would be better because your rook can use an open file.
flags.critique: 100cp and the reasons are pin, pin, overload — then the sentence talks about an open file and ignores them. Duplicate pin is a smell. If Qd4 is the wrong queen placement, say where she's clumsy; if Rad8 is better because it contests d, say that. 'Rooks like open files' is a poster, not a lesson.

flags.quote: Moving your pawn to c4 is the strongest move.
flags.critique: c4 hits the bishop on d5 and grabs space. The only reason is backward_pawn, which never even made the sentence — so I get a blank strongest-move and a hidden structure tag I can't see. Kick the piece. Don't mutter about backward pawns.

flags.quote: Moving your pawn to d6 is the strongest move.
flags.critique: No reasons, no idea. d6 solidifies e5 and asks the c8-bishop to come out. That's teachable in six words. 'That's the one.' on a quiet pawn move is how this whole game starts sounding like a slot machine.

flags.quote: Moving your pawn to a3 is the strongest move.
flags.critique: a3 prepares b4 against the c5-bishop. Two moves later you play b4 and still say nothing. If the coach can't connect a3→b4, I will never learn a plan that takes two moves.

suggestions.title: Don't call even recaptures undefended wins
suggestions.detail: wins_material currently emits 'the X was undefended' whenever SEE looks like winning the captured unit, so Nxd5/Bxd5/bxc6/Raxd1 all sound like free pieces. Require SEE after the full exchange on that square (or 'this capture recaptures') before that copy. A 1200 recaptures all game; they notice when you congratulate them for winning a defended pawn.

suggestions.title: Never explain a mistake with its upside
suggestions.detail: Qxd3 is an inaccuracy 'because the pawn was undefended'; Bxh6 is a blunder for the same reason. selectBecause / playedBecause is attaching capture and pin reasons from the played move to a negative verdict. For inaccuracy/mistake/blunder, prefer ignored_threat, hanging-after, or the suggested move's idea — never wins_material of the move you just called bad.

suggestions.title: Require the captured unit to actually defend
suggestions.detail: exd5 'takes the defender of Nc6' and gxf4/exf4 'take the defender of the bishop' are illegal geometry. Gate removed_defender on the captured piece attacking newlyHanging (pawns only diagonally forward). This is the difference between teaching tactics and teaching nonsense.

suggestions.title: Name saved pieces by origin, not destination
suggestions.detail: saves_piece uses the post-move unit, so Ba7 'saves your a7-bishop.' ownedPhrase should keep from-square (c5-bishop retreats) or drop the square: 'saves your bishop from b4.' Learners hear tautology immediately.

suggestions.title: Ban empty strongest-move on plan moves
suggestions.detail: a3, b4, d6, Rd3, Kf7, g5 rendered 'is the strongest move.' with no because. If reasons are empty, don't claim strongest — or add cheap detectors you already almost have: kicked_by_pawn for b4, a rook attacking a piece for Rd3/Rh7/Rh4, king_activity in queenless endings. The cadence 'That's the one.' on nothing is the aesthetic failure of this dump.

suggestions.title: Stop selling 'likely take a pawn' in openings
suggestions.detail: describeReason already special-cases reason.likely → 'you can likely take X.' That line is how Nf3's improvement becomes a fake snack on e5. Don't pick likely captures as the because for missed_improvement when the alternative is a pawn break; use center_control / 'you challenge the e-pawn.' The word likely is a tell.

suggestions.title: Don't lead with backward/doubled on the wrong moves
suggestions.detail: c4, f4, f5, bxc6, gxf4 dump backward/doubled/isolated while the sentence talks about something else or nothing. selectBecauseReasons already prefers tactics; extend that so pawn-structure kinds never outrank 'this pawn attacks that bishop' or 'you recapture, doubled c-pawns are the cost.' Jargon without the hit/cost is what a 1200 skips.

suggestions.title: Tag king marches as activity, not exposure
suggestions.detail: Kf7/Ke6/Kd5 are best centralizing moves tagged king_more_exposed and pawn_shield. Once queens are off, a short king_activity / centralizes_king reason (and copy: 'your king belongs in the center now') would fix a whole class of empty endgame plies. king_more_exposed should not fire on the side that's supposed to activate.

whatWorked: Castling copy on plies 14–15 actually teaches two jobs: king tucks, rook enters.
Nc6 'saves your pawn from capture' after Nf3 hits e5 is a real beginner lesson.
c5 'saves your pawn from capture' matches the queen sitting on d3.
Bf4 'saves your bishop from capture' after Rh7 is the one honest beat in the Bxh6 collapse.
Rh3+ naming a skewer of king and pawn is the rare tactic sentence that is true.
e4 unveiling Bd2 toward h6 is a fair discovered-attack kernel (buried under king_more_exposed).
